training_summary: The corpus reveals Roman Republican archaeology as fundamentally concerned with material culture transitions from ca. 509-27 BCE, encompassing excavation methodologies, site-specific investigations from Botromagno to Cosa, and the integration of numismatic, ceramic, and architectural evidence. The discipline bridges field excavation with broader questions of Romanization, urbanism, and cultural transformation across the Mediterranean.

key_works.facet_contribution: Provides comprehensive framework for Republican material culture studies, integrating excavation methodology with broader cultural questions
Exemplifies site-specific excavation methodology at Botromagno, demonstrating Iron Age to Republican transition through stratigraphy
Shows application of zooarchaeological methods to Roman Republican contexts, demonstrating interdisciplinary approaches
Demonstrates rural archaeology approaches and peasant material culture excavation at Pievina
Provides architectural and cultural interpretation of Roman urban spaces through archaeological evidence
